extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners and PRSA members (communications professionals, agencies, in-house teams)
extracted.subtask_description: Comprehensive ethical guidance from PRSA/BEPS for public relations practice, covering specific issues (pay-for-play, social media, plagiarism, influencers, native ads, AI accountability, leaks, billing, front groups) and how the PRSA Code of Ethics applies. Includes recommendations, professional values implicated, and procedural resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding the PRSA Code of Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRSA Code of Ethics exists to inspire ethical behavior, clearly identify improper public relations practices and teach members how to avoid them. It upholds core values including advocacy, honesty, expertise, independence, loyalty and fairness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRSA as a voluntary organization can: establish voluntary practice standards, inspire/educate best practice, promote voluntary compliance, establish ethical obligations for members, and set limited membership procedures. PRSA's enforcement authority is limited (no government sanctioning power). The Code identifies what is unethical or improper (a threat to ethical practice; behaviors inappropriate or inconsistent with the Code; disruptive behaviors that undermine ethical practices; practices destructive to reputations). Use the Code as an aspirational, guiding standard while recognizing limits of enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay-for-Play
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay-for-play: when payment is required for the development and publishing (in print or through digital channels) of content — blog posts, videos, interviews, podcast interviews, print or digital columns or interviews — creating a transaction where undisclosed payments are made to feature specific content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRSA/BEPS position: pay-for-play conflicts with PRSA Code provisions (Free Flow of Information; Disclosure of Information; Conflicts of Interest; Enhancing the Profession) and professional values (Honesty, Fairness, Independence). Because lack of transparency can deceive consumers, BEPS recommends: request and include disclosure with the final information product whenever compensation was provided in return for exposure; encourage disclosure of travel, lodging, gifts or non-monetary compensation; always encourage clear and obvious disclosure of crucial information consumers should know. Note FTC guidelines may require labeling as "sponsored content" in some contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics & Social Media
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media platforms are largely unmonitored and unregulated; their speed and accessibility create new ethical challenges that increase professional responsibility for organizations and practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS position: practitioners must not accept common social media practices at face value and should incorporate a higher standard by adhering to the PRSA Code. Four Code provisions apply: Disclosure of Information; Safeguarding Confidences; Conflicts of Interest; Enhancing the Profession. Specific guidance: content providers should fully disclose paid placements and all associations; safeguard confidential/private information (corporate, personal, IP); be aware of employees' NLRB-defined free speech rights; disclose conflicts of interest when communicating; when working with influencers/product samples require proper disclosures per FTC guidelines; ensure gifts are nominal, legal and infrequent; use social media to inform and share best practices while maintaining trust and credibility. BEPS recommends treating trust as the currency of social media and applying the cited Code provisions in all digital/social media use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism is the unauthorized use or close imitation of another's language and thoughts and representing that content as one's own original work; it can be intentional or inadvertent and differs from but overlaps copyright concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS position: inadvertent plagiarism carries equal weight to intentional misrepresentation. Practitioners must understand intellectual property rights and PRSA ethical standards on plagiarism. Applicable Code provisions: Free Flow of Information; Competition; Disclosure of Information; Conflicts of Interest. Professional values implicated: Honesty, Expertise, Fairness. Recommendations: do not copy content (sentence, paragraph, document) even if edited; use your own words and paraphrase rather than copying; when paraphrasing give proper credit; use quotation marks and credit exact wording; when using internet sources, acknowledge creators and give proper credit; disclose all sources for your work product. Recognize that fair use/open source claims do not absolve the need for attribution where representing others' work as your own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paid Spokespersons and Influencers
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone paid to serve as a spokesperson, advocate or influencer for an organization must disclose the contractual arrangement or relationship with the sponsoring interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS position: commercial relationships must be disclosed in advance of or simultaneous to the public forum so affected audiences can make informed decisions. Applicable Code provisions: Disclosure of Information; Conflicts of Interest; Enhancing the Profession. Values: Advocacy, Independence, Honesty, Fairness. Recommendations: every party in the contractual relationship must disclose the relationship; failure to disclose is improper conduct; be honest and accurate in communications, revealing sponsors for causes/programs and any financial interests; counsel that disclosures be clear and appropriately timed (advance or simultaneous). Follow FTC and platform rules regarding influencer disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representing Front Groups
rubrics_metrics.description: A front group is an organization created or labeled to mislead the public as to its true mission, often to hide true intent and create deception by hiding sponsors or goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS position: any effort to deceive the public or others is a clear violation of the PRSA Code of Ethics. Applicable Code provisions: Free Flow of Information; Disclosure of Information; Conflicts of Interest; Enhancing the Profession. Values: Honesty, Fairness, Advocacy. Recommendation: PR professionals must act in the public interest and uphold transparency; assisting front groups or individuals representing undisclosed sponsorships/deceptive descriptions — even if lawful — constitutes improper conduct and should be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overstating Fees or Compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Overstating charges, fees and/or compensation (claiming payment or credit for work never performed) harms clients and the profession and may violate contracts or law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS position: members should charge clients only for services rendered and in accordance with contracts and obligations; proper reporting of services rendered, time spent, out-of-pocket charges and related fees is required. Applicable Code provision: Enhancing the Profession. Values: Honesty, Fairness, Loyalty. Recommendations: adhere to a rigid code of conduct and highest standards of integrity; bill only for services performed and expenses actually incurred per existing contracts; do not inflate or overstate charges or supporting data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native Advertising & Sponsored Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Native advertising/sponsored content blends paid presence with organic content so that consumers may not distinguish between sponsored and editorial material; sponsorship should be clearly identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS position: make a clear distinction between organic content and sponsored content; the sponsor should be clearly identified. Applicable Code provisions: Disclosure of Information; Free Flow of Information; Competition; Conflicts of Interest; Enhancing the Profession. Values: Honesty, Advocacy, Fairness. Recommendations: ensure sponsorship is fully disclosed within the content's context and clearly apparent to consumers; disclosures should be clear and appropriate to the medium; sponsored content must be easily discernable from organic content and must not attempt to deceive consumers into believing it is independent or objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI and Leadership Accountabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: As AI and machine learning become integrated in organizations, ethical issues arise about assigning accountability for machine decisions and addressing errant outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS position: humans with oversight responsibility at the time of a machine's errant decision must be held accountable (not the machine); accountability should rest with people charged with oversight who are expected to identify root causes, corrective actions and provide transparency. Applicable Code provisions: Disclosure of Information; Free Flow of Information; Conflicts of Interest; Enhancing the Profession. Values: Honesty, Advocacy, Fairness. Recommendations: counsel senior leadership that AI cannot be held accountable; draw clear lines of human responsibility and present them forthrightly when developing communications and responses involving AI decisions; ensure leadership takes responsibility for root cause analysis, corrective actions and transparency to maintain ethical operation of AI systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Media as a Reflection of Majority Opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media activity is driven by a minority of very active users and is not a scientifically vetted indicator of majority public opinion; treating social media as representative can mislead audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS position: social media may provide insights but is not necessarily representative of the majority. Applicable Code provisions: Free Flow of Information; Disclosure of Information; Enhancing the Profession. Values: Honesty, Fairness, Advocacy, Independence. Recommendations: when sharing analysis based on social media, remind audiences that the platform is an informal, nonscientific source and may not reflect general public sentiment; present any social media-based conclusions with that context and caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Leaks
rubrics_metrics.description: PR professionals often have access to confidential/proprietary information; leaking unauthorized information to media or others undermines trust and can be illegal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BEPS position: members should refrain from leaking information without expressed approval of organizational leadership; leaking undermines trust and may be illegal with criminal/civil penalties. Applicable Code provisions: Safeguarding Confidence; Disclosure of Information; Free Flow of Information; Conflicts of Interest; Enhancing the Profession. Values: Loyalty, Honesty, Fairness, Advocacy. Recommendations: be aware of laws, regulations, contracts and business terms governing information flow; adhere to contractual/legal obligations and NDAs; never autonomously share information obtained in confidence; follow procedures for approving disclosures to internal/external publics.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEPS Handbook and Application (resources & roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: The BEPS Handbook outlines roles/responsibilities of BEPS Chair and members, PRSA Chapter Ethics Officer position description, historical timeline of the PRSA Code, and tips on integrating ethics into chapters/sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the BEPS Handbook as a procedural resource for applying the Code: consult role descriptions, chapter officer guidance, historical context, and integration tips. The page provides a link to download the full BEPS handbook and contact information (beps@prsa.org) and a reporting form for concerns. BEPS is volunteer-based and aims to respond in a timely manner (allow three weeks before re-contact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics Quiz (self-assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: A short quiz developed by BEPS to test one's Public Relations Ethics Quotient on contemporary issues (fake news, COVID-19, equity/equality, remote work challenges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The quiz is a member-only resource on the site for pressure-testing ethical decision-making under uncertainty. Use as a self-assessment tool to identify gaps; membership required to view/take the quiz.
